issues.legal_issue: Rental income received from property must be classified as business income when leasing the property is the company’s business.
material_facts: The assessee company owned property and received rent by leasing it.
The company’s business was leasing its property and earning rent, and it had stopped its other business activities.
The dispute in the appeals concerned whether the rental income was taxable as income from house property or as business income.
issues.conclusion: The rental income must be taxed under the head “Profits and gains of business or profession,” and not as income from house property.
issues.legal_principle: Applying Chennai Properties and Investments Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income Tax (2015) 373 ITR 673 (SC), the Court held that rental income is business income where letting the property is the assessee’s business. It referred to Karanpura Development Co. Ltd. v. CIT (1962) 44 ITR 362 (SC), which distinguishes ordinary letting from letting that is part of a trading operation, and held that Chennai Properties stated the correct law. The Revenue also relied on M/s. S.G. Mercantile Corpn. (P) Ltd. v. CIT, Calcutta (1972) 1 SCC 465; the Court did not treat that reliance as changing the result.

rule.if: tax_head_classification_appeal and company_owns_rented_property and company_business_is_leasing_property and rental_income_received

predicates.tax_head_classification_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in which the tax classification of rental income is disputed.
predicates.company_owns_rented_property: The company owns property that it leases to others.
predicates.company_business_is_leasing_property: Leasing its property is the company’s business.
predicates.rental_income_received: The company receives rent from leasing the property.

issues.definition: When an appeal disputes the tax classification of rent received by a company that owns rented property and carries on leasing as its business, the rental income is classified as business income.
